prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Two angles sit between the lines on the SAME side of the transversal, and they add to $180^\circ$. What are these angles called? (Any standard name for the pair is fine.)
hint: "Between the lines" gives you the word interior. Now describe where they sit relative to the transversal.

hints.text: "Between the lines" gives you the word interior. Now describe where they sit relative to the transversal.
They are on the same side, so the name starts with "same-side" (or the prefix "co-", or "consecutive").
They are co-interior angles, also called same-side interior or consecutive interior angles.

explanation: Both angles are between the parallel lines, so they are interior angles.
They are on the same side of the transversal, which is what "co-", "same-side," and "consecutive" all signal.
These are the one interior pair that is supplementary rather than congruent: they add to $180^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Three names, one idea
steps: Textbooks call this pair co-interior, same-side interior, or consecutive interior angles — all the same angles.
What matters is the behavior: on parallel lines they always sum to $180^\circ$.
